subject.title: fix(slack): apply default timeout to WebClient and write client options

question: Should Slack adopt blanket 30-second web and 60-second write-client deadlines, or require operation-specific deadlines that preserve file-upload behavior?
rationale: The values alter existing transport behavior across sends, uploads, lookups, reactions, and other API calls; source inspection establishes the risk, but repository product intent must determine which operation classes may safely fail on a fixed deadline.

options.title: Use operation-scoped deadlines
options.body: Apply bounded clients only to operations with defined timeout and retry semantics, while preserving or separately configuring file-upload transfers.

options.title: Accept global deadlines
options.body: Keep the shared defaults, but explicitly accept slow-upload and ambiguous-write risks and require real send/upload upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Pause this change
options.body: Leave shared client behavior unchanged until a concrete production hang and per-operation timeout policy are established.

recommendation.title: Use operation-scoped deadlines
recommendation.body: Apply bounded clients only to operations with defined timeout and retry semantics, while preserving or separately configuring file-upload transfers.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recently merged Slack timeout work contains the closest current-main design precedent and transport proof.
